source_text:
Fragmenta in epistulam ad Hebraeos
Hebr 1,12 Τοῖς ἀμφὶ τὸν Ἀβραάμ τε καὶ τὸν Μωϋσέα καὶ τοὺς καθ' ἑξῆς.
διαφόρως οὖν, φησί, καὶ καταλλήλως ἑκάστῳ καιρῷ τοῖς ἡμετέροις προγόνοις διὰ
τῶν οἰκείων προφητῶν ὁμιλήσας θεός, τοῦ παντὸς ἤδη χρόνου συμπληρουμένου
λελάληκεν ἡμῖν ἐν υἱῷ, τοῦτ' ἔστι νόμοις 421 πρότερον τὸ γένος ἡμῶν ἑκάστης
γενεᾶς καταλλήλοις πρὸς κτῆσιν δικαιοσύνης τε καὶ θεογνωσίας διὰ τῶν ἑαυτοῦ
δούλων παιδαγωγήσας, τῶν χρόνων ἤδη συμπληρωθέντων ἐν τῷ Χριστῷ καὶ τῇ
κατ' αὐτὸν οἰκονομίᾳ τὴν τούτων ἡμᾶς αὐτοτελῆ χάριν ἐυηγγελίσατο. λέγει δὲ τὴν
μετὰ τὸν σταυρὸν διὰ τῆς ἀναστάσεως αὐτοῦ πρὸς τὸ ἄφθαρτον καὶ ἀναμάρτητον
τῆς φύσεως τῆς ἡμετέρας ἀποκατάστασιν.
thought_title: God's speech to the ancestors and in the Son
orientation: The commentator opens by explaining Hebrews 1:1-2, where the author of Hebrews says God spoke to the ancestors through the prophets but has now spoken in the Son.
pass_a_gloss: To those around Abraham and Moses and those in succession. In various ways therefore, he says, and suitably to each season, God, having conversed with our ancestors through his own prophets, when all time was already being completed, has spoken to us in a Son, that is, having previously by laws suitable to each generation instructed our race for the acquisition of righteousness and knowledge of God through his own servants, when the times were already completed, in Christ and in the plan according to him he announced to us the complete grace of these things. He means the restoration of our nature after the cross through his resurrection to the incorruptible and sinless state.

choices.why: Glossary term for the restoration of human nature through Christ's resurrection.
Glossary term for God's plan of salvation accomplished in Christ.
αὐτοτελῆ means complete in itself, perfect; the grace of the gospel is full and self-sufficient.
The verb means to train or educate as a παιδαγωγός; 'instructed' keeps the educational sense without importing the Greek loanword.
The verb εὐαγγελίζω means to proclaim good news; the rendering keeps the gospel sense explicit.

bible_refs.note: διαφόρως ... τοῖς ἡμετέροις προγόνοις διὰ τῶν οἰκείων προφητῶν ὁμιλήσας θεός

pass_b_english: So God, he says, spoke to our ancestors in various ways, each suited to its time, through the prophets who belonged to them—to Abraham, Moses, and those who came after. But now that all time was reaching its completion, he has spoken to us in the Son. That is, he first instructed our race through his own servants by laws suited to each generation for acquiring righteousness and the knowledge of God. Then, when the times had been completed, he announced to us in Christ and in the plan accomplished through him the complete grace of these things. By this he means the restoration of our human nature after the cross, through his resurrection, to an incorruptible and sinless state.

last_rejected.quote: the complete grace of these things
last_rejected.why: Missing 'self-complete/perfect' sense of αὐτοτελῆ; 'complete' alone loses the nuance of grace that brings fulfillment to completion.
last_rejected.fix: the grace that brings these things to their perfect completion
last_rejected.ruling: αὐτοτελῆ rendered 'complete' captures the sense of perfection/self-sufficiency; nuance loss is preference, not major error
